To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
central banks should take a more proactive stance in the fight against climate change, and that this can be done without violating their mandates.
1) Central banks are mandated to promote sustainable finance, but only 12% of them explicitly have a sustainability mandate.

Central bank mandates and sustainability objectives are only partially aligned, as the majority of central banks do not have explicit sustainability mandates, and only 29% of central banks have mandates that explicitly support the government's sustainability policy priorities, including climate change policies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the mandates and objectives of central banks are sufficiently broad to incorporate climate related policies and green finance promotion.
how the current mandates of central banks can be interpreted to include sustainability objectives.
the question of how far central banks can go in their role as climate change policy makers and how they can best promote green finance and sustainability in general.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
central banks are mandated to promote green finance, but not to pursue climate mitigation policies.

central banks should be given a mandate to promote green finance and to incorporate climate risks into their policy frameworks, as these risks have a direct impact on their conventional core responsibilities of monetary and financial stability.

the current mandates of central banks are sufficient to enable central banks to incorporate sustainability and climate related risks into their core responsibilities and policies, but that the current mandate set-up is not sufficient to promote green finance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of central banks have not yet adopted sustainability objectives and mandates, but they should do so in order to fulfil their traditional core responsibilities.
climate change is not a new issue for central banking and that most central banks have the mandate and the capacity to take on climate change related risks and mitigation policy objectives.
central banks have a mandate to address climate risks, but not a mandate to promote green finance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the mandates and objectives of central banks are generally aligned with the promotion of green financing, there is still a need to strengthen the role of central banks in the promotion and implementation of sustainable development goals.

central banks should not be mandated to promote green finance or sustainability, as this would be inconsistent with the principles of monetary and financial stability and the central bank's role as a guardian of price and financial stability.

the majority of central banks are already in a position to incorporate climate risks in their core policy implementation framework and thus to contribute to the achievement of the Paris Agreement's climate objectives.
